title: Step 67-B Admin authentication context and dashboard contract readiness
description: HIGH-risk Backend/OpenAPI contract-readiness stage. Reconcile existing Admin login/FIDO/session/me/permissions/scopes/Step-Up success responses with actual AuthController/WebAuthn runtime and the global success envelope, regenerate typed OpenAPI output, sanitize GET /admin/auth/session so internal sessionId/permissions/scopes are not echoed there, remove the non-runtime /admin/dashboard operation from executable HTTP authority while preserving Product Design UNRESOLVED_NOT_GRANTED/unavailable-only evidence, and refresh only generator-equivalent Product Design provenance hashes caused by the canonical source changes. No database, dependency, Admin frontend or business-authorization mutation.

dependencies.evidence: PR #352 merged; exact-SHA Canonical CI #1710, Phase A #1209 and CodeQL #844 SUCCESS; terminal Lock release comment 6108601184.

transport_rules: Admin auth success payloads must match current controller return shapes; no frontend-local guessed models.
Permissions/scopes remain server-derived; typing them does not grant authorization.
No dashboard metric/count/feed contract is invented.
evidence.admin_session_privacy: SANITIZED_PUBLIC_STAFF_IDENTITY_ONLY; internal sessionId remains server-side for Step-Up; permissions/scopes use dedicated endpoints

acceptance_criteria.description: OpenAPI provides explicit success envelopes for existing Admin login, FIDO challenge/verify, Step-Up challenge/verify, logout, session, me, permissions and scopes operations based on actual controller values plus the global ResponseEnvelopeInterceptor. Existing Admin action POST runtime status remains 201 and is documented as such; no synthetic 202 success alternative remains.

GET /admin/auth/session is sanitized to expose only staff type/id/accountId in its success envelope. Internal sessionId remains server-side for Step-Up binding; permissions and scopes are available only from their dedicated typed endpoints.
Generated OpenAPI types expose the Admin success envelopes instead of content?: never and are byte-for-byte reproducible from canonical OpenAPI.

Login/pre-auth/admin-session bearer tokens remain cookie-only. No pre_auth_token or session_token enters JSON response schemas. Only the dedicated short-lived session-bound step_up_token is an explicit response payload.
WebAuthn challenge wrappers are typed at the stable wrapper boundary while nested options remain an extensible object owned by the WebAuthn runtime; no browser-option semantics are invented.

GET /admin/dashboard is absent from executable OpenAPI/generated paths because no runtime controller/permission authority exists; Step56 UNRESOLVED_NOT_GRANTED evidence remains preserved and no metric/count/feed is fabricated.
Only generator-equivalent Product Design provenance/hash artifacts change as a consequence of canonical OpenAPI/AuthController source mutation; no Product Design semantic state is promoted.
No database migration, dependency, Admin frontend, Storefront, RBAC/service business rule, dashboard runtime, analytics runtime, workflow or Current-State mutation is introduced.

HIGH-risk closure requires exact-head Canonical CI, Phase A, CodeQL/Security, deterministic Review, exact-artifact ACTIVE Lock, Project Owner Human Gate, protected merge, exact-SHA postmerge verification and terminal Lock release.

external_gate_evidence.rule: Step 67-B is HIGH risk. Exact-artifact Project Owner approval is mandatory after technical/security/review/Lock evidence is complete.

repair_history.root_cause: Removing GET /admin/dashboard from OpenAPI violated frozen Step56 operation-union and GAP-01/GAP-02 evidence, which intentionally retains this contract-only operation as UNRESOLVED_NOT_GRANTED.
repair_history.repair: Restore dashboard as contract inventory only with explicit x-eqcofe runtime=unresolved_not_granted and frontendConsumption=forbidden; preserve untyped response and no runtime authority.
